back.body: SCENE SIZE-UP, ALL FIVE OUT LOUD: BSI · safety · nature · number of patients · resources · GENERAL IMPRESSION → LEVEL OF CONSCIOUSNESS → AIRWAY → BREATHING → CIRCULATION · TREAT LIFE THREATS AS YOU FIND THEM, do not finish the survey first · STATE THE TRANSPORT DECISION · STRUCTURED HISTORY from the patient where possible · ASSESS THE COMPLAINT PROPERLY: onset, provocation, quality, radiation, severity, time · FULL VITAL SIGNS, THEN A SECOND SET — commonly lost when time runs short · FOCUSED EXAM guided by the complaint · REASSESS everything and the effect of what you did · THE COMMONEST CAUSE OF FAILURE ON ANY SHEET IS DOING THINGS SILENTLY — THE EXAMINER CANNOT SCORE WHAT THEY DID NOT SEE OR HEAR
back.why_it_matters: He checked scene safety by looking around the room. The examiner had no way of knowing.

back.body: BSI, STATED · GATHER cylinder, regulator, tubing, mask BEFORE you start · CHECK THE CYLINDER PRESSURE AND SAY WHAT IT READS — a scored step, and on a real call the one that stops you running out mid-transport · CRACK THE VALVE to clear the port where your programme requires · ATTACH THE REGULATOR, PINS ALIGNED, tightened · OPEN THE VALVE AND CHECK FOR LEAKS · ATTACH THE TUBING · PRE-FILL THE RESERVOIR BAG BEFORE THE MASK GOES ON — THE classic failure. The device is a BAG OF OXYGEN TO DRAW FROM, and a flat bag is a bag of NOTHING · APPLY AND SEAL the mask · SET THE FLOW SO THE RESERVOIR DOES NOT COLLAPSE on inspiration — if it collapses, the flow is too low · REASSESS

back.body: BSI INCLUDING EYE PROTECTION — this is splash work · OPEN THE AIRWAY MANUALLY FIRST: an adjunct HOLDS AN OPEN AIRWAY OPEN, it does not OPEN a closed one · ORAL AIRWAY ONLY WHERE THERE IS NO GAG REFLEX — IF THEY GAG, IT COMES STRAIGHT OUT, because a patient who gags can vomit · SIZE as your programme directs · NASAL AIRWAY IS TOLERATED WITH A GAG REFLEX — that is its advantage. Size, LUBRICATE, insert ALONG THE FLOOR of the nasal passage, bevel as directed. FORCE IS NOT PART OF THIS SKILL · SUCTION: MEASURE BEFORE YOU INSERT · IN WITHOUT SUCTION, OUT WITH IT · LIMIT EACH ATTEMPT · OXYGENATE BETWEEN ATTEMPTS — suction removes oxygen too
back.why_it_matters: In without suction, out with it. That is the whole skill.

back.body: BSI WITH EYE PROTECTION — the splash skill above all others · OPEN THE AIRWAY, ADJUNCT, SUCTION — the bag does not fix an obstruction · CORRECT MASK SIZE: A MASK THAT DOES NOT SEAL DOES NOT VENTILATE AT ALL. The air goes ROUND the mask · OXYGEN at the protocol flow · TWO-RESCUER TECHNIQUE WHENEVER YOU CAN — one holds with BOTH HANDS and thinks about nothing but the seal · VENTILATE AT THE PROTOCOL RATE AND SAY IT · JUDGE BY VISIBLE CHEST RISE — not the bag, not your effort · NO RISE? FIX THE POSITION, THE SEAL, THE OBSTRUCTION — before anything else · SQUEEZE SLOWLY AND SMOOTHLY: fast and forceful fills THE STOMACH, which then pushes on the diaphragm AND MAKES VOMITING MUCH MORE LIKELY
back.why_it_matters: The examiner said one word, which was slower. The chest started moving instead.

back.body: BSI AND SCENE SAFETY, STATED · CONFIRM UNRESPONSIVE, NO NORMAL BREATHING, NO PULSE — quickly. AGONAL GASPING IS NOT BREATHING, and it is the finding most often misread · COMPRESSIONS IMMEDIATELY, AND SEND FOR THE DEFIBRILLATOR AT THE SAME TIME · COMPRESSION QUALITY IS THE TREATMENT: depth · rate · FULL RECOIL (leaning stops the chest refilling) · MINIMAL INTERRUPTION · PERFUSION BUILDS OVER SEVERAL COMPRESSIONS AND FALLS THE INSTANT YOU STOP · AED ON AS SOON AS IT ARRIVES, FOLLOW ITS PROMPTS · PADS ON BARE, DRY SKIN · SAY CLEAR AND LOOK, BEFORE ANALYSIS AND BEFORE THE SHOCK — THE LOOKING IS THE PART THAT GETS DROPPED · RESUME COMPRESSIONS IMMEDIATELY AFTER THE SHOCK. NO PULSE CHECK · CHANGE COMPRESSORS — quality falls before you notice
back.why_it_matters: He said clear with his eyes on the machine. He had no idea what the other rescuer was doing.

ADD ON TOP AND PRESS HARDER — the clot is in the dressing you were about to remove · PRESSURE FAILING ON A LIMB → TOURNIQUET, PROXIMAL TO THE WOUND, TIGHTENED UNTIL THE BLEEDING STOPS · A TOURNIQUET TIGHT ENOUGH HURTS, AND THAT IS NOT A REASON TO LOOSEN IT — A HALF-TIGHT ONE STOPS THE BLOOD LEAVING WHILE ARTERIES KEEP FILLING THE LIMB, WHICH IS WORSE THAN NONE · NOTE THE TIME, SAY IT, WRITE IT, HAND IT OVER · SHOCK: position, oxygen, AND KEEP THEM WARM — COLD BLOOD CLOTS BADLY

back.body: FOR AN ISOLATED MID-SHAFT FEMUR FRACTURE · WHY IT WORKS: THE THIGH MUSCLES ARE THE STRONGEST IN THE BODY, and when the femur breaks they DRAG THE ENDS PAST EACH OTHER — causing pain, more damage, and SIGNIFICANT INTERNAL BLEEDING. Traction overcomes the spasm and reduces all three · CONTRAINDICATED: KNEE · HIP · PELVIS · LOWER LEG OR ANKLE ON THAT SIDE · PARTIAL AMPUTATION OR AVULSION. IF YOU CANNOT SAFELY PULL AGAINST THE ANKLE AND FOOT, YOU CANNOT USE IT · TWO PEOPLE, ALWAYS · MANUAL TRACTION FIRST, AND NEVER RELEASED UNTIL THE DEVICE TAKES OVER — keep saying you are holding it · MEASURE AGAINST THE UNINJURED LEG · TRACTION UNTIL THE PAIN AND SPASM EASE, not to a force · CMS AFTER
back.why_it_matters: He said still holding every twenty seconds. Nobody ever had to wonder.

back.body: BSI: EYE PROTECTION, GOWN AND MASK — the messiest thing you will do · IS DELIVERY IMMINENT? CROWNING IS THE ANSWER; the history is only supporting evidence · IMMINENT MEANS YOU DELIVER WHERE YOU ARE — driving gives you the same event with less room, less light and fewer hands · PREPARE BEFORE THE HEAD ARRIVES · SUPPORT THE HEAD WITH GENTLE COUNTER-PRESSURE: YOU ARE CONTROLLING THE SPEED OF SOMETHING HAPPENING ON ITS OWN, NOT PULLING · CHECK FOR A CORD AROUND THE NECK · SUCTION PER PROTOCOL — practice has changed · SHOULDERS ONE AT A TIME · THE BABY IS EXTREMELY SLIPPERY — BOTH HANDS · DRY, WARM, STIMULATE · NOTE AND SAY THE TIME · YOU NOW HAVE TWO PATIENTS AND THE MOTHER IS THE ONE WHO GETS FORGOTTEN
back.why_it_matters: Somebody deliberately turned round and looked at the mother instead.

back.body: PLAN THE ROUTE AND THE MOVE BEFORE YOU TOUCH THE PATIENT AND SAY IT OUT LOUD — fifteen seconds, and it prevents most of what goes wrong.
